fix_tasks.evidence_summary: Two lenses call this critical and both glitch hunters call it major. A flat, untextured light-grey polygon with stair-stepped edges sits at the massif foot in every pose, including rest and the UI frame: q00 x255-357 y376-408 (plus a sliver at 365-400, 409-420), std 11.7 vs 4.3 and Laplacian 5.5 vs 1.1. It moves with the plate: ptr_left 127-232/379-407, ptr_right 377-475/380-405, ptr_orb 240-345/417-447, p04 225-330/490-520, p06 210-320/526-557 (magnified, 2-3 px steps). It is crisp in sw_intro_1/3/5 and faint in sw_tau_*. A white 2-3 px tick about 20 px long appears on the navy far-left ridge only in non-rest views: ptr_right 224-238/332-351, ptr_top_right, ptr_bottom_right, ptr_orb 77-92/371-387, and the left-orbit spots at x0-15. The hold shows the same kind of crack: p06 31-80/472-522, sw_hold_L, sw_pop_B, sw_rel_BL, sw_intro_0. The ridge is 30-40 levels too dark and flat: crest box x10-120 y285-335 is 33,53,82 vs 64,88,124; rows 300-360 are a uniform 28,46,75 with sd 2.7 vs 17.2. The crest is at y about 257-260 vs 277-285.
fix_tasks.root_cause:
(a) The polygon is baked into the plates, not made by the shader. pipeline/raycast_plate.py traced it to the split that prep_v2/v3 made in Object_2.008 at y = 88: the vertex delete dropped the faces across the cut, and V2_Massif was then turned rigidly by 1.53 deg. Every v2-v5 plate therefore shows a gap onto terrain 132 m away plus the cut foot as a flat ledge at 103 m (n.z 0.95-0.99). The fpvar1 hidX probe shows it at the nodal 'top' spot as well, so the projector blend is not involved. (b) The white ticks are cracks in the 28 %-decimated V2_Ridge proxy (env_proxy.glb). PLATE_FRAG's crack rule (oz0 40-300 m, fz0 > oz0*1.02 + 0.5 -> uv0) only rescues cracks for the rest projector. The extra projectors (GLSL_PLATE_PROJECTOR_BLEND with

Visible PCF) see the backdrop through the same crack and paint their own texel there. The n100 test proxy (blend/proxy_v3) removed the streaks at ptr_top_right. (c) The ridge rock from prep_v4.py (ROCK_K 1.5, ramp 0.012-0.046) is darker than F000, and V2_Ridge still has its v2 height.

It started at 07:52, takes about 2 h, and writes blend/v2build7: prep_v6 centroid split with a 12 m fade of the massif turn, prep_v7 ridge heights x0.9, prep_v4b rock albedo x3.5 with snow streaks at 0.6, five plates in 4 strips each, and env_proxy.glb exported with full=V2_Ridge,V2_Massif. 2) Before publishing, compare crops of plate_rest.png and plate_hold.png against v2build5 and v6test/cmp_v5_v6.png. The SeenY lake fix from 07:15 (lab only) ships in this same deploy. 4) Verify with shoot_qc (all poses), shoot_pointer (all 10 spots plus the *_off views), shoot_sweep, probe_seam4 at rest/ptr_R/ptr_TR/ptr_orb/hold_L, and region_stats at q00. Pass criteria: the q00 box 255-357 x 376-408 has std <= 6 and Laplacian <= 2; no 1-3 px line in the ridge box (0-320, 300-420) at any ptr or hold spot (max luma <= crest median + 25); crest at y 272-285; crest box at least about 50,75,110 (otherwise T04 step 4 applies). 5) Check T0 performance on Iris 640 at scale 0.6. The bigger proxy (v2 was 155k tris, n100 358k) must keep rest at 30 fps or more and hold at 24 fps or more. If it does not, re-export with ratio=0.6 on V2_Massif only. 6) Contingencies: (i) if v7 fails, export_env_v3.py full=V2_Ridge,V2_Massif from the v5 scene (minutes, no render) fixes the cracks with the v5 plates; (ii) heal the polygon in all five v5 webps with a snow-to-mist clone (about 150,165,188, feathered 6-10 px); (iii) if a tick remains at ptr_right or ptr_orb, it is the boundary of prep_v4's screen-angle rock mask (tan -0.34..-0.27 from the rest camera, a world-space wedge whose snow side folds into view from orbP and tilt). fix_tasks.title: Lake and plate blend at in-between cameras (pop, release, hold with pointer): filtered mirror lengths and soft visibility, so no stair-stepped slab reflections, boxy rock halo, floe mosaic, ghost rock or mound wedge
fix_tasks.evidence_summary: Pop and release (glitch hunter, major): in sw_pop_B the reflection columns at x966-988 y577-648 and x1270-1300 y585-655 are 1-3 px stair-steps; the slab reflection's lower edge at 1290-1420 x 607-627 is stepped; the rock at 1146-1230 x 610-627 has a white rectangular halo with a square dark notch. This shows in all six pop frames and mildly in sw_rel_TR. The same slabs are clean at rest and at full hold. In sw_rel_L/BL (30-80, 534-576) the left floe breaks into a 4-8 px square mosaic. In sw_rel_BL the floe face at 1060-1122 x 675-710 is smeared and the rock at 1022-1100 x 725-766 has a pale ghost. In ptr_left, ptr_top_left and ptr_bottom_left (1165-1218, 398-432) a smooth pale-blue wedge continues the right mound's flank over the far peak. Small fringes: sw_hold_R/TR (1370-1385, 573-592) has a 1-2 px white crescent on the right-edge rock, and p06 (503-522, 533-545) has a comb of light texels on the hill silhouette.
fix_tasks.root_cause:
Off every projector (pop camera z about 5.5, release z about 9.7, hold with the pointer orbited), Water.ts re-aims every lake lookup through plateMirrorPoint /

MirrorPoint. These read the mirror-ray length L = textureLod(u

Depth, uv, 0).b from a NearestFilter HalfFloat 1536 px map (bakeProjector). L is constant per depth texel and jumps at slab-reflection edges, so the re-aimed columns step by whole texels. At a projector itself the straight lookup is used, which is why rest and full hold are clean. The blend weights are also binary per texel: visK = 1 - smoothstep(0, 2.5, behindK) from a single nearest tap; the 'straight' bool; the quv/kq fallbacks (step()); and 'raised' (one tap, smoothstep 0.05-0.12 m). A raised texel gets lod = lodX + 5.0*raised, a 5-mip average of rock, snow and water: the boxy pale halo, shaped like the depth texel. In the plate, plateUnoccluded searches in 4-texel steps (sx = texel*4); filled fragments read lod +3 and nofill fragments lod +4. Near disocclusions that neither rest nor orbN sees, this gives 4-8 px blocks and a smooth 4-mip copy of the occluder's neighbourhood (the wedge). CameraRig.orbitGain springs back at omega 2.5 during the release, so by p07 the camera has already swung about 1.6 deg off the hold axis (holdK about 0.32).
fix_tasks.implementation_plan:
0) Do this after T01 (the new proxies change every depth map). First attribute each artefact with the pipeline/probe_envvar.mjs debug tints (fill state, per-projector weight, raised, nofill) on the crops above. 1) Filtered L: in plateMirrorPoint and GLSL_EXTRA_MIRROR, replace the single .b tap with a manual 2x2 bilinear lookup on texel centres (u

DepthTexel). Skip taps with L <= 0. When max/min of the valid taps exceeds 1.25 (an edge), use the minimum (the nearest reflector) instead of the weighted mean. 2) Soft visibility: visK =

Visible(muv, fz) (the existing 5-tap PCF) times the 2.5 m ramp; for rest, vis0 uses plateVisible the same way. Replace the 'straight' bool with straightW = 1 - smoothstep(0.0, 1.5, sBehind) and blend the straight and re-aimed lookups by it. Turn the kq/quv fallbacks into smoothstep(0.03, 0.08, seenY - y) mixes. 3) Raised: evaluate it at the four bilinear texels and blend. Change lod +5.0 to +2.0, and move plateW 0.6*raised toward the live mirror, as occl already does. 4) Plate fill near the camera: for fz < 40 m, run plateUnoccluded's first 12 horizontal steps at 2 texels (then 4) and give near-field filled fragments lod +4. For nofill fragments with extra coverage < 0.05, mix 50 % toward MIST_COLOR*0.85 instead of showing the 4-mip copy. 5) CameraRig: change the orbitGain release omega from 2.5 to 1.6 (holdK at p07 about 0.25). 6) Re-run probe_time/t06time (SeenY), then probe_glitch at every pop, rel and hold spot. Lake shader compile on ANGLE should stay under about 2 s, and RAM must stay inside the watchdog (fixed taps only, no new loops).
fix_tasks.risk: Medium. It adds 3 taps x 2 iterations per projector in the lake, for up to five projectors when off-projector. Measure T0 fps at pop and release (target 30 or more at scale 0.6) and the ANGLE compile time. The min-L rule can pull a reflection column 1 texel toward the nearer reflector; check the floe pillars at q00 against F000. The slower orbit return delays the pointer response for about 1 s after a release; run probe_interact.

fix_tasks.title: Frame-edge and bottom-strip polish: cursor-lens colour fringe, dark pockets in pitched-down poses, small rim fringes
fix_tasks.evidence_summary: sw_pop_B (690-750, 735-760): faint orange/pink arcs in the ripples just under 'Scroll to Explore'. ptr_bottom (1237-1320, 743-766): a dark-navy rounded pocket, white '//' slivers (1325-1340, 750-762) and a navy band (1342-1420, 751-766). ptr_bottom_left: the pocket at 1327-1400 x 732-758, white speckle at 1332-1407 x 758-766, a 6x8 px grey square at 1334-1340. ptr_bottom_right: 1130-1215 x 754-766. Rock bases revealed in the overscan have rough 1 px stair-steps and pixelated reflections (ptr_bottom_left 713-750/726-766, ptr_bottom_right 430-553/717-766). The client's rule is nothing odd at the bottom of the frame.
fix_tasks.root_cause: (a) PostChain GRADE_FRAG computes ca = uChromatic*dot(c,c)*0.02 + lens*0.0025. The pop's chromatic kick was removed (pp.chromatic = 0), but the cursor-lens term remains. During a mouse hold, HeroEngine sets lensStrength = s.hold, so the 40 px disc under the pointer splits R and B by about 0.9 px over high-contrast ripple crests; pop_B's pointer sits at the bottom centre. (b) The ptr_bottom family are pure pans at the rest position (EL_TRAVEL 0, EL_PAN 0.75), so only plate_rest is sampled. The pocket, slivers, grey square and speckle are therefore the plate's own bottom overscan rows (rest-y about 770-795) as Cycles rendered them. PLATE_FRAG's near-field lift (shK = nearK*(1 - smoothstep(0.02, 0.12, ln)), x1.25) is too weak for a recess at luma about 0.03.
fix_tasks.implementation_plan: 1) In GRADE_FRAG, set ca = uChromatic*dot(c,c)*0.02 and drop lens*0.0025; the lens keeps its magnify and frost. 2) After T01 publishes v7, retouch plate_rest.webp in the bottom overscan only (rest-frame y < 0): lift the pocket's black point to about 58,86,124 with a soft top-down gradient so it reads as a recess, and clone out the slivers, the square and the speckle. Keep the retouch as a layer and re-apply it after any re-bake, or fold it into T18. 3) Shader safety net in PLATE_FRAG, only where restFrame(uv0).y < 0.0 and d < 12 m: for luma < 0.05 use lt = 0.05*pow(l/0.05, 0.7) with 30 % desaturation, and lod +0.6, because overscan rock edges render rougher than the frame. 4) Only if 2-3 are not enough: limit panDown in CameraRig.setAspect to an explicit 0.15 deg so the frame bottom stays above rest-y 770. This is a last resort because it shrinks the downward pan. 5) The crescent (sw_hold_R/TR) and the p06 hill comb: use T02's tints and ?proj=0 to check whether they are in plate_hold itself. If they are baked, soften those few pixels in the plate; otherwise T05's hold DOF covers them.
fix_tasks.risk: Low. The plate retouch has to be redone after every re-bake. The overscan-only lift cannot reach the rest frame (restFrame y >= 0). No tier cost; removing the CA saves 2 taps while the lens is active.

It hides the foothill ridge (340-575, 545-595) and wraps the iceberg base (1050-1320, 560-610). The engine has only a thin uniform veil. The fog band (0-560, 560-600) is 157,172,192 vs 146,162,183 with no structure. Massif upper slopes (180-330, 380-450) are 154,169,189 vs 132,151,184. Rows 440-480 at x60-400 are 141-149,159-166,183-188 vs 116-127,137-145,167-175: the reference brightens about +30 from rock into fog, ours about +5. leftmtn p1 is 112 vs 74. Far floe fronts (460-1440, 615-645) are 144,163,188 vs 169,186,208, and the near floe undercuts (375-640, 705-720) are near-black. The water band has p1 74 vs 121 and Laplacian 9.5 vs 4.2: no depth of field, while F420's mountains and foreground are defocused. Hold p99.9 is 243 vs 253. fix_tasks.root_cause: (a) plateBank in GLSL_PLATE_MIST (shared by plate and lake) is hold*smoothstep(60, 120, d)*step(d, 330)*(1 - smoothstep(1, 18, y))*(0.55 + 0.45*wisp), mixed toward uFogColor*(0.44, 0.54, 0.66) at min(bank*0.75, 0.68). That is a linear height ramp with no top edge, one slow wisp, one colour, and nothing nearer than 60 m, so the far floes (40-60 m) and the iceberg foot miss it. (b) The massif keeps most of its rest haze in the hold: aerial 0.24*(1 - 0.6*uHold), slopeH 0.15 and fog*(1 - 0.33*uHold) lift the rock 18-26 levels. (c) The linger is integrated in HeroEngine (uFogHold = max(camExpand, fh - dt/1.5)). shoot_qc and shoot_sweep use pose() then settle(1.6 s), which decays it to camExpand (0.257 at p07, 0.052 at p08) before the shot, so no capture can show the linger; live it would be 0.78/0.62. 1.5 s is also shorter than the reference's linger. (d) uDofBlur = 1.5 and uFocusRange = 30 m: at the hold focus (12.7 m), floes and water at 15-30 m get at most 0.6 mip, and the near term 1.6*(1 - smoothstep(8, 16, d)) ends before the hold frame's bottom (about 18 m). (e) The berg grade (x1.5 chroma, x0.82 luma) has no uHold term.
fix_tasks.implementation_plan: Tune after T01 (v7 plates) and T04. 1) Deterministic linger: add a Choreography driver fogHold (not in BLENDED). In expand it is camExpand. On release, store {at: now, from: camExpand}; in release and in idle it is max(camExpand, from*(1 - smoothstep(0.6, 2.0, now - at))). A debug pose 'release' at t sets at = now - t. HeroEngine sets uFogHold = d.fogHold and drops the dt integration. Expect p07 and p08 at about 0.97, and the bank gone by about 2 s. 2) Bank shape, in the plate and in Water's mix line: top = 11.0 + 4.0*fbm(p.xz*0.015 + vec2(uTime*0.02, 0.0)) m; height = 1 - smoothstep(top - 6.0, top + 2.0, y); billow = 0.6 + 0.4*fbm(p*0.035 + drift at 0.4 m/s, 3 octaves, 2 on T0); distance ramp smoothstep(35, 90, d) for y < 3 m and smoothstep(60, 120, d) above; opacity min(bank*0.85, 0.8). Colour = mix(uFogColor*vec3(0.30, 0.37, 0.46), uFogColor*vec3(0.44, 0.54, 0.66), billow), so the lows are darker swirls. Targets at p06: band (0-560, 560-600) about 146,162,183 with sd >= 6; top edge at y about 470-500 and soft (no line under a 3.5x luma stretch); foothill ridge and iceberg base veiled. 3) Massif in the hold: aerial x(1 - 0.85*uHold), slopeH x(1 - 0.7*uHold). For d 100-330 m and y > 12 m: col = mix(col, (l + (col - l)*1.15)*0.9, uHold). Targets: rows 440-480 about 120,140,170, with the fog about +30 brighter than the rock above. 4) Near floe undercuts (d < 30 m, luma < 0.12): lift by x(1 + 0.6*uHold) toward uFogColor*0.35. Far floes come from the bank's near ramp; their darkest pixels should be >= 115. 5) Iceberg: berg *= 1 - 0.5*uHold, plus 12 % desaturation in the hold (target 78,108,144). 6) Hold DOF: in PLATE_FRAG lodDof and Water lodX use focusRange = mix(uFocusRange, 10.0, uHold); near term 1.6*(1 - smoothstep(8 + 10*uHold, 16 + 12*uHold, d)); mountains stay at 1.5 mip. Target Laplacian of the water band (y640-766) about 4-5. There must be no paper-cut (a crisp proxy edge around a blurred interior) at p06 (90-450, 320-520) or on the floes; if one appears, lower the near term to +1.0. 7) After T06 and T09, check that hold p99.9 is >= 250 from the slit and cap glints. fix_tasks.title: Orb light carried by the ice, plus a luminous orb cap, so the orb never goes dark behind a band
fix_tasks.evidence_summary: The orb lens calls this critical; it is the Awwwards jury's #2 and a minor composition issue. At p06 the orb reads as a clear soap bubble or pearl. In the hero window (470-970 x 150-570), pixels at 245 or above are 113 vs F420's 1970, and at 235 or above 1708 vs 8164. sw_hold_L has 58 px at 235 or above and sw_hold_TR 538. In the idle loop, q01 has 1700 vs 7003, sw_tau_0.75 has 640 and sw_tau_2.75 has 1119, against 6813-9179 at tau 0.25/2.25/3.75, so the orb visibly switches off every 4 s. Glow-area ratios vs the reference are 0.52/0.24/0.72/0.73 at F000/F015/F030/F045. p04 has a hot spot (2106 vs 979 px at 245+) but half the spread (2808 vs 5541 at 235+). F420 shows a white-cyan slit between the lips (650-830, 415-440) and a cyan-white cap with glints (690-770, 285-300); in loop F015 the band glows white-mint. z_orb_p06_vs_p05.png shows B's near band covering the core at p06, while at p05 the portal pose leaves the core visible.
fix_tasks.root_cause: This is light transport, not emission. Orb.update keeps the hold gain at (1 + 0.1e + 0.1h)(1 - 0.3h), about 0.94 (uGain about 2.3 vs 2.5 at rest), and portal does not affect it. (1) The ice sees the orb only through the refraction copies. BLIT_FRAG compresses everything above 0.8 as m' = 0.8*sqrt(m/0.8), so a core at 16 becomes 3.6 and 6 becomes 2.2. ICE_FRAG then divides by (1 + 0.12*max), desaturates 15 % above tl 0.8-2.5 and 25 % overall, and tints and absorbs. A band in front of the core therefore reads as a pale grey, about L200-215. (2) Round 7 turned off the analytic 'lantern' term; lantern now only lowers scatter (s *= 1 - 0.5*lantern). (3) The orb's own emission is concentrated in the middle: the fill follows coreK = pow(1 - smoothstep(0, 0.97, bImp), 0.6) (about 0.15 at bImp 0.85), the hot core sits within bImp 0.55, and the cyan limb is 0.28*uGain. The cap and lower arc that show around a band are the orb's dim outer zone over the refracted panorama, so they read as an empty glass shell. (4) Bloom only sees the compressed light through the ice, so no halo leaks.
fix_tasks.implementation_plan: 1) Ice: an orb-light floor, as in pipeline/icevar50.mjs g50a/g50b/g50c, inserted before the uEnergy line in ICE_FRAG. For fragments in front of the orb: lanternG = exp(-(dRay/(sigma*0.8255))^2); glowC = vec3(0.80, 0.97, 1.0)*uOrbGlow*k*lanternG*mix(0.55, 1.0, max(frost, max(tirZone, pathK))); col += glowC*clamp((lum(glowC) - lum(col))/lum(glowC), 0, 1). The floor only fills where the transmitted image is darker, so the clear eye band at q03 (L195 vs 195) stays. Start with g50a (k 0.9, sigma 1.15) and compare g50b (1.26, 1.35) and g50c (adds a 0.05 prox frost scatter). Then raise k until the lantern centre peaks at about 2.2-2.6 scene-linear, so the env bloom band (threshold 2.0) lets a soft halo through. 2) Orb (Orb.ts), a luminous outer zone during the hold: uRim = clamp(2*h, 0, 1) with h from Orb.update's hold argument. The limb term becomes 0.28 + 0.3*uRim, plus a mint floor col += vec3(0.75, 1.0, 0.95)*0.35*uGain*smoothstep(0.55, 0.8, bImp)*(1 - smoothstep(0.93, 0.99, bImp))*(1 - fIn)*uRim. Optionally add a sun glint on the shell: ggxSpec(N1, -rd, uSunDir, 0.08)*uSunColor*fIn. Target: the p06 cap above the band at L 235 or more, with a few glints at 250 or more. 3) Hold slit: retune after T09's lips. fix_tasks.root_cause: ICE_FRAG refracts with Nr = normalize(mix(Ng, Nf, 0.85) + (N - Nf)*0.4), where Nf comes from chiselNormal(): Voronoi cells (CELL 9/1.975, about 0.22 m, about 18 px at rest), each tilted by rnd*0.16 right up to a crisp border (keep = smoothstep(0, 0.04 + aa, e)). Each cell bends the view by up to about ±0.03 rad x uLens 0.35 x uLensDepth 6 m, so it shows its own patch of the copy shifted about 10-15 px, with a hard edge: the mosaic. The only blur is lod = mix(0, 1.6, rough) on a half-res copy (about 6 px at most), and only frost patches (noise A) trigger it. At grazing angles, macroW = smoothstep(0.35, 0.75, 1 - dot(Ng, V)) adds back the full wall tilt, so band tops and bottoms swing far across the half-res copy and give stretched, stair-stepped strips. fix_tasks.title: Ice silhouettes: lumpy, chiselled outlines and broken end caps (subdivision plus sharper displacement), and a frost micro-surface
fix_tasks.evidence_summary: The ice lens calls this critical, as does the Awwwards jury (#1). Ring D's top arc at q00 (600-860, 210-245) is a perfectly round, uniform tube; the reference outline is wavy and chiselled, with a lump every 15-20 px and mottled frost. Detail in 660-780 x 214-238: mid-frequency 1.47 vs 4.16, low-frequency 2.50 vs 6.16, so the engine is 2.5-2.8x smoother. q01 ring D's flank (560-660, 180-560) is a smooth gel tube where the reference is notched and glints. End caps are flat planes with straight edges (p06 810-860, 150-240; the q02 band ends at 870-910, 335-400) where the reference's are broken, bevelled and chipped. The p04 pop segments read as acrylic blocks with flat clean cut faces (about 930-1035 x 290-410 and 380-465 x 430-540). The p06 arcs show faceted low-poly silhouettes.
fix_tasks.root_cause: The ring meshes in hero.glb are low-poly: an A quarter has 1088 triangles, a B half 4096, C and D 2112 each, about 0.1 m per segment along the ring. ICE_VERT's displacement (iceHeight, a 2-octave fbmd at 5/1.975 with about 0.4 m wavelength and ±uDisplace 0.099/2, about ±0.05 m, plus a 0.01 m crease) is sampled only about 4 times per bump, so the outline stays a smooth circle. Cut faces keep the mesh's planar caps, and the superellipse slab (n = 8) squares the section. The fragment's chisel cells only tilt normals and do not change the silhouette.
fix_tasks.implementation_plan: Start from pipeline/icevar52.mjs. sub1 is a midpoint subdivision (x4 triangles, indexed and welded). sil1 adds a sharper height field (3 fbm octaves plus ridged chips at 2.2x the scale) and a tangential displacement along the ring of ±4.5 cm, so caps break while the sides only slide along themselves. sil2 is sil1 with 1.35x the amplitude. 1) Choose by the q00 top-arc detail (targets: mid-frequency about 4, low about 6) and by the cap shapes at p06 and q02. 2) Build it in: subdivide once at load in the Rings constructor, after the hero-frame transform and before ringAxis and the section measurement, on T1 and T2 only (ring triangles about 16.8k -> 67k). T0 keeps the original mesh and height field. 3) Frost micro-surface in ICE_FRAG, in object space so it does not swim: a fine bump from vnoise(vObjPos*60) (2-4 px features at rest) at strength 0.1-0.2, gated by T07's veil and frost and faded by fwidth. It breaks the broad sheen into small glints. 4) Specular after the geometry change (round-7 T22): rSpec = mix(0.12, 0.34, smoothness) with smoothness = 1 - keep*length(tilt), so only chip faces get tight lobes. 5) Checks: A's joints stay closed at rest (uJoined; the displacement depends on pr + uNoiseOffset, so it is continuous across pieces); the back-depth pass uses the same ICE_VERT; re-run probe_holdbounds because the silhouettes grow; the p06 caps no longer read as flat white quads.
fix_tasks.risk: Medium-high. Ring triangles go up 4x across the mirror, back-depth and both colour passes (about 335k triangles per frame on T1); keep T1 (Iris Xe class) at 50 fps or more, or subdivide only B, C and D. Larger displacement can open joints or make the thin D intersect itself. Round 6 read strong low-frequency wobble as melted wax, so keep the normal wobble at 0.18 or lower. Do this after T07 and T11 so the silhouette is judged with the final material.

fix_tasks.title: Release snap (F453) and pop (F358): gaps on the diagonals around one tilted torus, and B as one long bar

Inside, a second partial ring of B plus 2-3 offset open arcs (570-900, 210-570) form a spiral, while F453 has one thick C/D torus (550-895, 260-520; bbox aspect about 0.75, i.e. about 40° of tilt). The glitch hunter sees a flat, coplanar bullseye/spiral in every rel_* frame, with B's two halves at different radii. p04: B is split into two short pieces (upper end 530-600/230-290, lower end at 915/575), about 20-25 % short, where the reference has one continuous bar from (500-580,170) to (940,625), about 600 px, longer than B's diameter of about 440 px. A is about 100 px tall vs 125-135, and the left chunk sits 45 px low.
fix_tasks.root_cause: (1) A's in-plane phase lock (tune.aPhaseOn, inside `if (d.expandPose > 0)`) is weighted by min(1, wE) and fades with expandPose during the release (0.36 at p07). The gap angles at the snap are therefore whatever the hold phase plus the tumble produce. (2) splitB is still 0.1 at F453 (RELEASE_RETURN sampled at t + 0.08), so B's halves sit ±0.05 m apart. uJoined (distanceSq < 1e-6, abs(q.w) > 0.99999) shows the cut whenever they are not exactly home. (3) C and D get different residuals at the snap: C Q_RES[2] 70° about X x bandInner 0.57 (about 40°), D dRelSnapDeg 38° about (1, 0.35, 0). The two ellipses are offset, which reads as a vortex. (4) At the pop the halves split along world Y while B's bar runs at about 49° (POP_AXIS[1]), so each half moves off the bar's line by 0.66 of the split, about as much as it moves along it.
fix_tasks.implementation_plan: 1) Phase lock during the release: weight it by max(wE, d.gapA) and target aPhiStar + tune.aRelPhaseDeg. Start aRelPhaseDeg at +30° and flip the sign if the gaps move the wrong way. Keep the same unwrap and tanh limit; MAX_TURN still bounds it. Target gaps at 1:30, 4:30, 7:30 and 10:30 at p07. 2) RELEASE_RETURN offset t + 0.08 -> t + 0.12 (splitB about 0.03 at p07); uJoined tolerance distanceToSquared < 4e-4 and abs(q.w) > 0.9999. 3) Give D the same snap residual as C: dRelSnapDeg 38 about (1, 0.35, 0) -> 40 about X, so C and D nest into one tilted torus (bbox about 550-895 x 260-520). 4) Pop: during popPose, split B's halves along the bar. dirSplit = normalize(mix(worldY, barAxisWorld, popPose)), where barAxisWorld is B's in-plane direction perpendicular to POP_AXIS[1]; latch the cut across the bar before the pop, spinCutAcross-style. Hand back to world Y as popPose returns to 0. Target bar length about 560-600 px. Left chunk vertical offset -0.22 -> -0.05 m. 5) Run probe_interact (15°/frame or less, including a press during the release) and the sweep rel_* and pop_* frames.
fix_tasks.risk: Low-medium. A phase correction that stays on through the release can add a visible in-plane turn; keep it under MAX_TURN and blend it out with gapA. The pop's split-direction change lasts about 0.3 s but must hand over to the hold's world-Y lips without a jump.

disagreements:
1) Why the orb is dark in the hold. Composition and the Awwwards jury say the emission drops when portal goes to 0 and ask to keep the energy on. The orb lens says it is a light-transport problem. The code agrees with the orb lens: Orb.update's gain, (1 + 0.1e + 0.1h)(1 - 0.3h), is about 0.94 in the hold and ignores portal. z_orb_p06_vs_p05.png shows B's near band over the core at p06; at p05 the portal pose leaves the core visible. Call: fix the light carried by the ice and add a luminous cap (T06), set the lips (T09), and leave the orb gain alone.
2) Ring thickness. Composition wants C/D's cross-section doubled and B's raised 25 %. The ice lens measured the tubes as right (D 28 vs 30 px). Call: no geometry change for C/D. The 'thin glass hoops' read comes from seeing front and back edges through clear ice plus crisp rim lines, which T07 and T11 fix in the material. Re-measure B afterwards and add 15 % to its axial section only if it is still under 32 px.
3) Hold radius. Composition says to push the arcs out 15-25 % (60-100 px). F420's quarter centroids sit at about rest radius, while ours are pulled in by 0.2-0.74 m (holdCompact 0.82, aOutBase -0.22). Call: return to about rest radius plus 0-0.4 m per slot, which is +60-100 px from where they are now, not beyond rest.
4) Raising the cluster. Composition offers 'lift the rig or lower the camera'. Lowering the camera would misregister the frozen hold projector (plate_hold). Call: lift the hero, uOrbCenter included, by 0.34 m x camExpand and never move the camera.
5) Grazing refraction. The ice lens wants the offset faded to 0; round 7's macroW gave the band ends their structure (sd 18 vs 15). Call: cap the offset at 12 px and add blur at grazing angles instead of zeroing it (T07).
6) Bloom. The grade lens asks for a higher threshold, the orb lens for a tighter radius, and the Awwwards jury for lower intensity on the core. The current thresholds (env band 2.0/1.5, orb band 7.0) and strength 0.1 measure close to the reference everywhere except the halo's tint and reach. Call: trim the far UP_WEIGHTS and tint the orb band mint (T13), and keep the thresholds.

Call: a hold-only near-field DOF with a narrower focus range, mountains unchanged (T05). It is safe now that the hold camera sits on its projector and v7 has undecimated massif and ridge proxies; verify there are no cut-outs.

9) Fog after release. Both judges saw the fog gone at p07/p08. Part of that is the capture method: shoot_qc and shoot_sweep run pose() then settle(1.6 s), which decays the integrated uFogHold to camExpand (0.257/0.052) before the shot; live it would be 0.78/0.62. Call: make the linger a deterministic Choreography driver and lengthen it to about 2 s (T05).

Call: v7 first (rock albedo x3.5, snow streaks, heights x0.9), then the shader haze ramp with a left-to-right gradient and no fog bank on the ridge in the hold (T04).
